source_input: Client use case 2, 'Device Upgrade Automation': "Devices upgraded along with space clear, firmware upload, post and pre checks along with scheduler option." Use case 10, 'Cisco ACI Upgrade Automation': "Managing upgrade of ACI chassis as per process suggested by Cisco." The client's aim is "to do automation using Claude for all these content".
why_this_course: Upgrades are routine maintenance that teams still run by hand at two in the morning. NIST frames patching and upgrading as preventive maintenance that should be operationalized, not improvised [c7]. Load balancer and fabric upgrades are where that is hardest: each vendor has its own space requirements, boot model and HA order [c1][c3][c4][c5].

Most failed windows come from the same few causes: not enough disk (NetScaler needs 7 GB free in /var [c4]), an unverified image [c2], the wrong HA order [c1][c3], a missing backup, or a window that runs out mid-pair while sync and mirroring are degraded [c2][c3]. Each one can be checked by code before the window opens.

This course teaches teams to let Claude read the fleet, draft plans and explain diffs, while deterministic code performs every space clear, install and reboot behind a ServiceNow approval. That split follows OWASP's guidance on limiting agent permissions and requiring human approval for high-impact actions [c37]. The client also asked for Cisco ACI upgrades done the way Cisco prescribes, which the course covers with Cisco's own validator and order [c20][c21].

design_decisions.decision: One vendor-neutral lifecycle across F5, NetScaler, Alteon and ACI
design_decisions.rationale: The client asked for space clear, firmware upload, pre and post checks and a scheduler; a single lifecycle lets the same runner and guardrails cover every vendor.

design_decisions.decision: Include one Cisco ACI module in a multi-vendor course
design_decisions.rationale: Use case 10 asks for ACI upgrades 'as per process suggested by Cisco' and has its own dedicated course; here one module shows how ACI fits the same lifecycle, following Cisco's pre-upgrade checklist and validator [c20][c21] rather than inventing a process, and leaves depth to the dedicated ACI course.

design_decisions.decision: Space clear is its own module with allowlists and dry run
design_decisions.rationale: Disk space is the client's first named step and a top failure cause; vendor guidance lists exactly what can be cleared [c15][c10].

design_decisions.decision: Golden snapshot and diff instead of ad hoc post-checks
design_decisions.rationale: A versioned snapshot makes the post-check objective and gives the change record clear evidence.

design_decisions.decision: Scheduler reads approved windows from ServiceNow
design_decisions.rationale: The client asked for a scheduler option; tying it to change windows [c28] stops runs outside approval.

design_decisions.decision: Claude proposes, code executes, a human approves every destructive step
design_decisions.rationale: Reboots and deletions are high impact; OWASP recommends human approval and minimal permissions [c37].

safety: Read-only tools by default; destructive steps only through the runner with an Approved change
Credentials only in environment variables or the lab vault
Shared DevNet sandbox used for read calls only
Reset scripts restore every device each evening

modules.title: The device upgrade lifecycle and why upgrades fail
modules.goal: Learners can describe how each vendor really upgrades and map every step to one vendor-neutral lifecycle before writing any automation.
learning_objectives: Learners can compare F5, NetScaler, Alteon and Cisco ACI upgrade mechanics
Learners can name the classic failure modes and the step where each shows up
Learners can map a vendor runbook onto the lifecycle: inventory, pre-check, space clear, upload, install, post-check, rollback, report
Learners can explain the course pattern: Claude plans and explains, code executes, a human approves, everything is logged

lessons.title: F5 BIG-IP: boot locations and UCS
points: Images go in /shared/images and install to an inactive boot location with tmsh install sys software image <iso> volume HD1.x [c1]
The source must be on 15.x or later to go to 17.5.1.4, so older systems need more than one hop [c1]
Save a UCS in /var/local/ucs and copy it off the device before upgrading [c1][c11]
Volumes report active, version, status and default boot location, which is how you know where you are [c9]
Install takes roughly three to seven minutes; failures are written to /var/log/liveinstall.log [c1]

lessons.title: NetScaler: /var/nsinstall and build files
points: Builds are copied to /var/nsinstall/<release>/build_<build>, extracted and installed with ./installns [c14]
./installns --pre_check runs the pre-upgrade validation before the real install [c14]
/var needs 7 GB free and /flash at least 250 MB [c4]
Upgrade one major release at a time, for example 12.1 to 13.1 to 14.1 [c4]

lessons.title: Radware Alteon: image banks and no config rollback
points: Back up the configuration and run the Upgrade Advisor Tool against the current config and target version [c5]
31.x to 33.x upgrade directly; older versions need intermediate hops [c5]
Configuration rollback is not supported: rollback means factory config for next boot, select the old image, reboot, upload the saved config [c5]
Some older Radware device families also need an upgrade password tied to the base MAC address; confirm for your Alteon model [c6]

lessons.title: Cisco ACI: controllers first, then switch groups
points: APICs are upgraded before switches [c20]
Since 4.0(1) there is one switch update group type; upgrade one switch of each HA pair at a time [c20]
The pre-upgrade validator runs when an update group is configured; a standalone script adds checks [c20][c21]
All switches must be Active under Fabric Membership before starting [c20]

lessons.title: Why upgrades fail and the lifecycle
points: Full /shared or /var: the image is uploaded but the install has no room [c4][c15]
Corrupt or unverified image: always check the vendor checksum before install [c2][c8]
HA pair in the wrong order: upgrade the standby or secondary first [c1][c3]
Missing backup or a backup left only on the device [c1]
Window overrun: F5 notes mirroring does not work until all devices run the new version, so a half-done pair is exposed [c2]
NIST frames upgrades as routine preventive maintenance to be operationalized, not ad hoc work [c7]

instructor_demo: Show the F5 volume list on lb-f5-01 through GET /mgmt/tm/sys/software/volume and tmsh show sys software
Show df -h on a NetScaler and point at /var usage against the 7 GB requirement
Walk the vendor runbooks side by side on screen
Fill the lifecycle map live with learner input
Show a failed install entry in /var/log/liveinstall.log from a recorded fixture
Explain the operating pattern and who does what at each stage

lab.brief: Walk a real F5 and NetScaler upgrade runbook by hand in the lab, record every step and decision, and map each to the lifecycle stages.
steps: Read the F5 and NetScaler runbooks provided
On lb-f5-02 (standby) list volumes and images and record the current version
Save a UCS and copy it to the lab file server
On lb-ns-02 (secondary) check /var and /flash free space
Run ./installns --pre_check on the staged build and record the output
Record each decision point (go or stop) and who would make it
Map every step to a lifecycle stage on the template
Mark every point where one of the classic failures would appear
success_criteria: Every runbook step is mapped to a lifecycle stage
Each classic failure mode is placed on the map with its detection point
Version, disk space and backup location are recorded for both devices
Decision points name the approver role

common_pitfalls: Treating the vendor upgrade guide as optional reading
Forgetting multi-hop paths when the source is old
Leaving the only backup on the device being upgraded
Assuming Alteon can roll back configuration like F5 or NetScaler

knowledge_check.q: Where does an F5 install go?
knowledge_check.a: To an inactive boot location (volume), for example HD1.2, while the active volume keeps running.

knowledge_check.q: How much free space does NetScaler need in /var for an upgrade?
knowledge_check.a: 7 GB: 1 GB for the bundle, 2 GB for extraction and 4 GB for the process.

knowledge_check.q: What is the rollback path on Alteon?
knowledge_check.a: Set next-boot config to factory, choose the previous image, reboot and upload the saved configuration.

knowledge_check.q: In ACI, what is upgraded first?
knowledge_check.a: The APIC cluster, before any switches.

modules.title: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP for upgrade workflows
modules.goal: Learners build a workbench where Claude sees the fleet only through typed read-only tools.
learning_objectives: Learners can install Claude Code and write a CLAUDE.md for the upgrade runner
Learners can build an MCP server wrapping F5, NetScaler, Alteon and APIC read calls
Learners can make every tool return validated typed output
Learners can separate what the model may propose from what code may do

lessons.title: Claude Code and project conventions
points: Install with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash; use claude -p for scripted runs [c32]
Project instructions in ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, shared through source control [c42]
Record hostnames, version matrix location, naming rules and red lines (no install, reboot or delete tools)
Keep the file short and specific so it is followed [c42]

lessons.title: Agent SDK scaffold
points: Define tools with @tool and register them with create_sdk_mcp_server [c33]
Tool names become mcp__upgrader__get_version and must be listed in allowed_tools [c33]
Return structuredContent and isError: true on failure [c33]
Pre-approve read tools only; anything else must prompt or be absent

lessons.title: Read-only device tools
points: F5: GET /mgmt/tm/sys/software/volume and /mgmt/tm/sys/software/image for versions, boot locations and images [c9][c8]
NetScaler: GET /nitro/v1/config/hanode for HA state and sync [c18]
Alteon: software and facts through the Radware SDK management functions [c38]
APIC: log in with POST /api/aaaLogin.json, then read-only class queries [c24]
Cyber Controller for centrally managed Alteons is an option; confirm its API with Radware before building on it

lessons.title: Strict schemas and the propose-versus-do line
points: Every tool output is a Pydantic model validated before it is returned [c31]
Mark tools with readOnlyHint, but remember annotations are only hints and enforcement stays in code [c34]
The model may propose plans and explain; only the runner may call write endpoints
Plans the model proposes are JSON validated against a schema [c35]

instructor_demo: Create the repo and CLAUDE.md live
Write get_version for F5 against a recorded volume response
Write get_ha_state for NetScaler and show the typed output
Register the server and ask Claude to describe the fleet
Ask Claude to reboot a device and show there is no tool to do it
Show a tool returning isError when a device is unreachable

lab.brief: Build the read-only MCP server, connect it to Claude Code and ask Claude to describe the fleet using only tool results.
steps: Clone the starter repo and set up a virtual environment
Write CLAUDE.md with conventions and red lines
Implement get_version, get_images and get_ha_state for F5
Implement get_version and get_ha_state for NetScaler
Implement get_version for Alteon against recorded responses
Implement get_firmware_status for APIC against the DevNet sandbox or recorded responses
Validate every output with Pydantic and add tests
Ask Claude to describe the fleet and check each statement against tool output
success_criteria: All tools return validated typed output
Claude's fleet description matches tool output with no invented facts
No write tool exists in the server
Unreachable devices produce isError results, not guesses

common_pitfalls: A generic shell tool that bypasses the read-only design

knowledge_check.q: What is the full tool name Claude sees for get_version on server upgrader?
knowledge_check.a: mcp__upgrader__get_version.

knowledge_check.q: Are MCP tool annotations enforcement?
knowledge_check.a: No; they are hints, and clients should not rely on annotations from untrusted servers.

knowledge_check.q: Which F5 endpoint lists boot locations?
knowledge_check.a: /mgmt/tm/sys/software/volume.

slides_and_assets: Recorded device responses for all four vendors

modules.title: Inventory and pre-flight discovery
modules.goal: Learners reconcile CMDB records with live device facts into one typed inventory and readiness report.
learning_objectives: Learners can query ServiceNow CMDB load balancer tables through the Table API
Learners can collect version, HA role, sync state and disk usage per vendor
Learners can express the target version matrix and upgrade paths as data
Learners can have Claude summarize readiness and flag CMDB mismatches

lessons.title: CMDB as the starting list
points: Load balancers live in cmdb_ci_lb and classes such as cmdb_ci_lb_bigip and cmdb_ci_lb_netscaler [c26]
Query with GET /api/now/table/cmdb_ci_lb_bigip?sysparm_query=...&sysparm_fields=name,ip_address,... [c25]
Page large results with sysparm_limit and sysparm_offset [c25]
Record owner and support group for each device for later approvals

lessons.title: Live facts per vendor
points: F5: active volume version and build, images present, HA state [c9][c8]
NetScaler: master state Primary or Secondary and sync status from hanode [c18]
Alteon: software version through SDK management info [c38]
Disk usage: /shared on F5 and /var and /flash on NetScaler against vendor minimums [c4]

lessons.title: The inventory model
points: One Pydantic model: hostname, vendor, platform, version, ha_role, sync_state, disk, license_ok, owner, cmdb_sys_id [c31]
Validation errors are reported per device, not hidden [c31]
A mismatch field records where CMDB and the device disagree
Each record keeps the raw source responses by reference so reviewers can check values

lessons.title: Version matrix and paths as data
points: targets.yaml: vendor, platform, target version, allowed source versions
Path rules: F5 17.5.1.4 needs 15.x or later at source [c1]; NetScaler one major release at a time [c4]; Alteon older than 31.x needs hops [c5]
The planner reads paths from data, never from the prompt
Each device gets READY, NOT READY or NEEDS HOP with reasons

lessons.title: Claude summarizes readiness
points: Claude reads the inventory and writes a per-device readiness summary
Every NOT READY device gets a plain-English reason tied to a field
CMDB mismatches are listed for the CMDB owner, not fixed by the agent
Summaries cite inventory fields by name so a reviewer can check every claim

instructor_demo: Query CMDB for lab load balancers and show the JSON
Collect live facts from the lab fleet
Show a CMDB mismatch on lb-ns-03 role
Load targets.yaml and compute readiness
Ask Claude to explain each not-ready device

lab.brief: Generate the readiness report for a mixed lab fleet and have Claude explain every device marked not ready.
steps: Write the CMDB query for the lab tables
Implement live-fact collectors for each vendor
Write targets.yaml with lab target versions
Implement readiness rules from the matrix
Ask Claude for explanations and review them against data
Write tests with recorded CMDB and device responses
success_criteria: Every lab device appears with readiness and reasons
CMDB mismatches are listed
Path rules come from data files
Tests pass offline

common_pitfalls: Trusting CMDB HA role without checking the device

knowledge_check.q: Which table holds F5 BIG-IP CIs?
knowledge_check.a: cmdb_ci_lb_bigip.

knowledge_check.q: Why keep upgrade paths in data?
knowledge_check.a: So they are reviewed, versioned and enforced in code rather than depending on the model.

knowledge_check.q: What happens to a CMDB mismatch?
knowledge_check.a: It is reported to the CMDB owner and blocks readiness until resolved; the agent does not fix it.

modules.title: Pre-checks and the golden snapshot
modules.goal: Learners capture a versioned snapshot and backups before any change and stop the run when anything is red.
learning_objectives: Learners can collect virtual server, pool, HA, certificate and licence state
Learners can take and verify backups on each vendor
Learners can define a versioned JSON snapshot schema
Learners can enforce hard stop rules

lessons.title: What goes in the snapshot
points: Virtual servers and their status, pools and member status, monitors
HA role, failover state and config-sync status [c18][c39]
Certificate expiry for bound certificates
Version, active volume and licence validity [c9]

lessons.title: Backups before change
points: F5: tmsh save sys ucs <name> writes to /var/local/ucs [c11]; download it with GET /mgmt/shared/file-transfer/ucs-downloads/<name> [c13]
NetScaler: POST /nitro/v1/config/systembackup?action=create with level full [c17]
Alteon: export and save the configuration before upgrade [c5]
Copy every backup off the device and record a hash of the file

lessons.title: Snapshot schema
points: snapshot_id, device, captured_at, schema_version, sections{}
Stable sort order so diffs are meaningful
Stored in the repo or artifact store, not only on disk
Secrets and session tokens are never written into a snapshot

lessons.title: Hard stop rules
points: Any red pre-check stops the run
No backup or an unreadable backup stops the run [c1]
Sync not in sync on an HA pair stops the run
Claude may explain the stop but cannot override it

instructor_demo: Capture a snapshot of lb-f5-01 and lb-f5-02
Save and download a UCS
Create a NetScaler backup through NITRO
Corrupt the backup file and rerun to show the stop
Ask Claude to explain the stop reason

lab.brief: Implement the pre-check and snapshot module with pytest coverage, then break a backup on purpose and watch the run stop.
steps: Implement UCS save and download for F5
Write pytest cases for pass and stop paths
Break the backup and confirm the run stops
success_criteria: Snapshot saved with schema version and ID
Backups exist off-device with hashes
A missing or corrupt backup stops the run with a logged reason
Tests cover each stop rule

common_pitfalls: Backups left only on the device
Treating warnings as passes without a rule

knowledge_check.q: Where does tmsh save sys ucs write?
knowledge_check.a: /var/local/ucs.

knowledge_check.q: What does the run do if a backup is missing?
knowledge_check.a: It stops; no backup, no upgrade.

knowledge_check.q: Why version the snapshot schema?
knowledge_check.a: So post-check diffs compare like with like after the schema changes.

modules.title: Disk space clearing and firmware staging
modules.goal: Learners free space safely from allowlisted paths and stage verified firmware.
learning_objectives: Learners can identify safe deletions per vendor
Learners can produce a dry-run space plan with sizes
Learners can upload firmware and verify its checksum
Learners can execute only approved, allowlisted deletions

lessons.title: Safe reclamation per vendor
points: F5: delete old images with tmsh delete sys software image <name> or DELETE on /mgmt/tm/sys/software/image [c10][c8]
F5: remove old UCS archives with delete ucs after confirming off-device copies [c11]
NetScaler: clear /var/core and /var/crash unless needed, /var/nsinstall except current firmware, /var/tmp/support bundles [c15]
NetScaler: /var/nstrace is the most common cause of a full disk [c15]
Alteon: remove stale images only per Radware guidance for your model

lessons.title: Allowlists and dry run
points: Allowlist per vendor of directories and file patterns
Never delete the running image or the image in the active or default boot location [c9]
Dry run lists each file, size and total freed
Claude drafts the plan from disk facts; code checks every item against the allowlist

lessons.title: Firmware upload
points: F5: POST /mgmt/cm/autodeploy/software-image-uploads/<iso> lands in /shared/images with Content-Range chunking [c13]
NetScaler: copy the build to /var/nsinstall/<release>/build_<build> [c14]
Check free space against the vendor minimum before upload [c4]
Resume interrupted uploads by chunk rather than restarting from zero [c13]

lessons.title: Checksum verification
points: Compare a locally computed hash with the vendor-published checksum; F5's upgrade guide uses md5 [c2]
F5 also reports checksum and verified for each image [c8]
Store the hash in the run state
Stop on mismatch and delete the bad upload

instructor_demo: Fill /var on the lab NetScaler with fixture files
Run the dry-run plan and show totals
Show an item refused because it is outside the allowlist
Approve and execute
Upload the F5 image and verify the checksum

lab.brief: Fill a lab device disk, run the dry-run plan, approve it and stage the firmware image with checksum verification.
steps: Fill the lab disk with the fixture script
Ask Claude to draft the space plan
Validate the plan against the allowlist
Obtain approval on the lab change
success_criteria: Free space meets the vendor minimum
Only allowlisted files were deleted
Firmware checksum matches the vendor value
All actions logged with approval reference

common_pitfalls: Deleting the image on the rollback volume
Deleting core files someone is investigating

knowledge_check.q: What is the most common cause of a full NetScaler disk?
knowledge_check.a: Trace files in /var/nstrace left running.

knowledge_check.q: Which F5 endpoint accepts image uploads?
knowledge_check.a: /mgmt/cm/autodeploy/software-image-uploads/, writing to /shared/images.

knowledge_check.q: What does the dry run show?
knowledge_check.a: Every file to be deleted, its size and the total space freed.

modules.title: Upgrade execution adapters, HA-aware
modules.goal: Learners build a runner that installs to the inactive location, upgrades HA pairs in the right order and can resume after failure.
learning_objectives: Learners can install and reboot on each vendor through API or CLI
Learners can order HA upgrades correctly
Learners can make steps idempotent and resumable
Learners can run only an approved structured plan

lessons.title: Vendor install steps
points: F5: tmsh install sys software image <iso> volume HD1.x, or POST to /mgmt/tm/sys/software/image; watch status on the volume [c1][c9]
F5: reboot into the new volume with the reboot option or by setting the boot location [c10]
NetScaler: POST /nitro/v1/config/install with url and Async to get a job id, then reboot [c16][c19]
Alteon: set the image for next boot and reload, following the release notes [c5]

lessons.title: HA ordering
points: Upgrade standby or secondary first and verify [c1][c3]
F5: run sys failover standby on the active to move traffic [c12]
NetScaler: force failover so the upgraded node becomes primary [c3]
Upgrade the former active, then confirm sync [c39]
Expect sync and mirroring limits while versions differ [c2][c3]

lessons.title: Idempotent and resumable
points: State file per run: step, device, status, timestamps, request ids
Each step checks current state first: if the target volume already runs the target version, skip
Resume from the last completed step after a crash
Rollback path recorded before each destructive step

lessons.title: Plan in, actions out
points: Claude proposes the ordered plan and exact calls as JSON validated against a schema [c35]
The runner executes only the approved plan hash
Any deviation stops the run
Human approval required before install and before each reboot

instructor_demo: Show the plan JSON for an F5 pair
Run install on the standby and watch status
Reboot and verify version
Fail over and upgrade the former active
Kill the runner halfway and resume

lab.brief: Upgrade an HA pair of lab load balancers end to end through the runner, with a mocked failure halfway to test resumption.
steps: Implement F5 install, reboot and failover steps
Implement NetScaler install and reboot steps
Run on the F5 lab pair
Inject a failure after the standby reboot
success_criteria: Standby upgraded and verified before failover
Both units on target version and in sync
Resume continues from the right step
No step outside the plan ran

common_pitfalls: Not waiting for install status complete before reboot
Assuming sync is normal while versions differ

knowledge_check.q: Which unit is upgraded first?
knowledge_check.a: The standby or secondary.

knowledge_check.q: How does NetScaler async install report progress?
knowledge_check.a: It returns an install id tracked with show ns job.

knowledge_check.q: Why record state after every step?
knowledge_check.a: So a failed run can resume or roll back from a known point.

modules.title: Post-checks, verification and rollback
modules.goal: Learners compare the post-upgrade state with the golden snapshot, get a structured verdict and execute rollback when needed.
learning_objectives: Learners can diff post and golden snapshots
Learners can get a structured pass, warn or fail verdict
Learners can execute vendor rollback paths
Learners can generate an evidence pack

lessons.title: The diff
points: Same schema as the golden snapshot so sections compare directly
Version must change; virtual servers, pools and members must not degrade
HA sync may show changes pending until the peer is upgraded; treat as expected only in that window [c2][c3]
Certificate expiry should be unchanged

lessons.title: Structured verdict
points: Claude reads the diff and returns verdict, reasons and rollback recommendation as JSON matching a schema [c35]
Code applies hard rules first: any fail rule overrides the model
The verdict text goes into the change record
A warn verdict needs a named human to accept it before the run continues

lessons.title: Rollback paths
points: F5: boot back into the previous volume, which is still installed [c9][c10]
F5: restore configuration with load ucs if needed [c11]
NetScaler: reinstall the previous build retained in /var/nsinstall [c14][c15]
Alteon: factory config next boot, previous image, reboot, upload saved config [c5]

lessons.title: Evidence pack
points: Pre and post snapshots, diff, verdict, logs and approvals
Attach to the change record with a PATCH work note [c25]
Store hashes of each file in the pack
Name the pack with the change number and run id so audits can find it

instructor_demo: Diff a clean upgrade
Diff a broken one with a pool down
Show the verdict JSON
Roll back the broken device
Generate the evidence pack

lab.brief: Run the post-check diff on a successful and an intentionally broken upgrade, then execute the rollback path for the broken one.
steps: Ask Claude for the verdict on both runs
Execute rollback for the broken device

citations.title: Installing BIG-IP Version 17.5.1.4
citations.key_fact: The source system must run 15.x or later; the .iso goes in /shared/images; save a UCS in /var/local/ucs and copy it off the device, upgrade the standby first and only then the active, turn off mirroring, and install with tmsh install sys software image <iso> volume HD1.x to an inactive location; watch progress with tmsh show sys software and read failures in /var/log/liveinstall.log.

citations.title: BIG-IP System: Upgrading Software (device group upgrade)
citations.key_fact: A device is forced offline before upgrade (it terminates connections and accepts no new ones, and the state persists across reboots on 11.1.0 and later); mirroring does not work until every device in the group has rebooted onto the new version, so F5 recommends a maintenance window; preparation includes verifying the .iso with an md5 checksum and checking RAID health.

citations.title: Upgrade a NetScaler high availability pair
citations.key_fact: Upgrade the secondary first, confirm with show ha node that it is secondary with synchronization disabled, run force failover so it becomes primary, then upgrade the former primary; when builds have different internal HA versions, synchronization and propagation are disabled until both match.

citations.title: Before you begin (NetScaler upgrade)
citations.key_fact: /var needs 7 GB free (1 GB bundle, 2 GB extraction, 4 GB upgrade) and /flash needs at least 250 MB; NetScaler recommends upgrading one major release at a time (for example 12.1 to 13.1 to 14.1) and backing up and removing /var/customizations before upgrading.

citations.title: AlteonOS 33.5.2.0 Release Notes: Upgrade Path
citations.key_fact: Back up the configuration and run the Upgrade Advisor Tool (updated database) before upgrading; 31.x to 33.x upgrade directly while older versions need intermediate hops; configuration rollback is not supported, so a version rollback means setting the next-boot configuration to factory, selecting the old image, rebooting and uploading the saved configuration.

citations.title: Updating Device Software (Radware device web help v6.13)
citations.key_fact: This Radware device help page requires an upgrade password from Radware tied to the base MAC address and the software file size, a saved configuration before upgrading, and lets the operator choose whether to enable the new version immediately; the device then reboots and the console confirms the version.

citations.title: SP 800-40 Rev. 4: Guide to Enterprise Patch Management Planning
citations.key_fact: Published April 2022, it defines enterprise patch management as identifying, prioritizing, acquiring, installing and verifying patches, updates and upgrades, and frames it as preventive maintenance to be operationalized with an enterprise strategy.

citations.title: APIRef_tm_sys_software_image
citations.key_fact: /mgmt/tm/sys/software/image lists images (resource methods GET, DELETE, POST) with properties build, checksum, fileSize, product, verified (yes if the image is authentic), version and volume.

citations.title: APIRef_tm_sys_software_volume
citations.key_fact: /mgmt/tm/sys/software/volume reports each boot location with active, version, build, basebuild, product, status (complete, installing and so on) and /media/default-boot-location.

citations.title: sys software image (tmsh reference)
citations.key_fact: tmsh install sys software image takes create-volume, reboot and volume options; list image can show checksum and verified; delete image removes named images or all; mirrored volume names must begin with MD1.

citations.title: sys ucs (tmsh reference)
citations.key_fact: save ucs <name> writes the running configuration to /var/local/ucs/<name>.ucs; load ucs restores it (options include no-license and passphrase); list ucs and delete ucs manage archives in /var/local/ucs.

citations.title: sys failover (tmsh reference)
citations.key_fact: run sys failover standby makes the active unit standby so its peer becomes active; run failover also supports offline and online.

citations.title: Demystifying iControl REST Part 5: Transferring Files
citations.key_fact: Image files upload with POST /mgmt/cm/autodeploy/software-image-uploads/ to /shared/images/; UCS archives download with GET /mgmt/shared/file-transfer/ucs-downloads/ from /var/local/ucs/; transfers are chunked with Content-Range: start-end/filesize and anything over 1M must be chunked.

citations.title: Upgrade a NetScaler standalone appliance
citations.key_fact: Run save config and copy ns.conf off the box, create /var/nsinstall/<release>/build_<build>, copy and extract the build .tgz, run ./installns --pre_check for pre-upgrade validation and then ./installns; the installer asks whether to delete old signature files and kernel images, and NetScaler advises answering No in most cases.

citations.title: How to free space on /var directory
citations.key_fact: Check with df -h and free space when /var reaches 90%; /var/nstrace is the most common cause of a full disk; clear /var/core and /var/crash unless recent investigation needs them; clear /var/nsinstall except the firmware currently in use; delete unneeded support bundles in /var/tmp/support.

citations.title: install (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: POST /nitro/v1/config/install takes a mandatory url for the build file (http, https, sftp, scp, ftp or file://), y to skip the reboot prompt, dontreboot, and Async, which returns an install id to track progress with show ns job.

citations.title: systembackup (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: POST /nitro/v1/config/systembackup?action=create makes a .tgz backup with filename, level (basic or full, default basic), includekernel and comment.

citations.title: hanode (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: hanode exposes the read-only master state (Primary, Secondary, UNKNOWN), hastatus (ENABLED, STAYSECONDARY, STAYPRIMARY, DISABLED), hasync and the reason for any HA sync failure.

citations.title: reboot (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: POST /nitro/v1/config/reboot reboots the appliance; warm: true restarts the NetScaler software without rebooting the operating system.

citations.title: Cisco APIC Installation and ACI Upgrade and Downgrade Guide: Pre-upgrade checklists
citations.key_fact: The APIC pre-upgrade validator runs automatically when an update group is configured and a standalone script can be run on the APIC; export the configuration with AES encryption first; APICs are upgraded before switches; since 4.0(1) there is a single switch update group type; upgrade one switch of each HA pair at a time; all switches must be Active under Fabric Membership.

citations.title: ACI Pre-Upgrade Validation Script
citations.key_fact: Copy aci-preupgrade-validation-script.py to the APIC (suggested /data/techsupport), run it with python, give admin credentials and the target version (which must already be on the APIC), and act on every FAIL or MANUAL CHECK REQUIRED result; output totals PASS, FAIL - OUTAGE WARNING, FAIL - UPGRADE FAILURE, MANUAL CHECK REQUIRED, N/A and ERROR.

citations.title: ACI Pre-Upgrade Validation Script: Validation reference
citations.key_fact: Checks include target image and MD5, APIC cluster Fully Fit, switch fabric membership, NTP, switch upgrade group guidelines, APIC and switch disk and /bootflash usage; the built-in validator runs during APIC or switch upgrades, and the Pre-Upgrade Validator app was deprecated in ACI 6.1(2); APICs are upgraded first prior to switches.

citations.title: ACI Sandboxes
citations.key_fact: The Always-On ACI Simulator sandbox accepts APIC API requests at any time with no reservation, as a shared instance.

citations.title: ACI Programmability: Getting Started
citations.key_fact: APIC REST authentication is POST /api/aaaLogin.json with an aaaUser object holding name and pwd attributes.

citations.title: Table API
citations.key_fact: The Table API provides GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE on /api/now/table/{tableName}; GET filters with sysparm_query (for example field=value^ORDERBYfield), trims with sysparm_fields and pages with sysparm_limit and sysparm_offset; POST inserts one record and returns 201.

citations.title: Load balancer fields and probes (CMDB tables)
citations.key_fact: Load balancer CIs are stored in cmdb_ci_lb with classes such as cmdb_ci_lb_bigip (F5 BIG-IP) and cmdb_ci_lb_netscaler (Citrix NetScaler), plus related tables cmdb_ci_lb_pool, cmdb_ci_lb_pool_member, cmdb_ci_lb_service, cmdb_ci_lb_interface, cmdb_ci_lb_vlan and cmdb_ci_lb_appl.

citations.title: Ask for Approval action
citations.key_fact: Ask for Approval takes a record, table, approval and rejection rules and an optional due date, and outputs an approval state (Requested, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled, No Longer Required, Skipped); running several Ask for Approval actions on the same record in parallel branches is discouraged.

citations.title: Change Management API
citations.key_fact: The sn_chg_rest Change Management API creates change requests (one per call) and runs conflict checks (GET /api/sn_chg_rest/change/{sys_id}/conflict); change records carry start_date and end_date for the planned implementation window, and change model states include New, Scheduled, Implement, Review and Closed.

citations.title: Events that trigger workflows
citations.key_fact: schedule runs on the latest commit of the default branch in UTC (optional IANA timezone), no more often than every 5 minutes, and may be delayed or dropped at high load such as the top of the hour; workflow_dispatch accepts typed inputs and needs the workflow file on the default branch.

citations.title: APScheduler 3.x User guide
citations.key_fact: APScheduler has triggers, job stores, executors and schedulers; persistent job stores survive restarts, SQLAlchemyJobStore on PostgreSQL is recommended when free to choose, and misfire_grace_time decides whether a missed run still executes.

citations.title: Pydantic: Models
citations.key_fact: Pydantic models validate data on creation or through model_validate and model_validate_json, raising ValidationError when data cannot be parsed into the model.

citations.title: Claude Code overview
citations.key_fact: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool for the terminal, IDE, desktop and browser; on macOS, Linux and WSL it installs with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash, and claude -p runs it non-interactively for scripts and CI.

citations.title: Give Claude custom tools (Agent SDK)
citations.key_fact: Python tools are defined with @tool, wrapped with create_sdk_mcp_server and passed in mcp_servers; their names are mcp__{server_name}__{tool_name} and are pre-approved through allowed_tools; tools can set readOnlyHint, return structuredContent and return isError: true on failure.

citations.title: MCP schema reference: ToolAnnotations
citations.key_fact: ToolAnnotations provide readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint; all are hints, not guarantees, and clients should never make tool-use decisions based on annotations from untrusted servers.

citations.title: Structured outputs
citations.key_fact: JSON outputs send a JSON schema in output_config.format (type json_schema) so the response matches the schema, and strict tool use (strict: true) guarantees schema validation of tool names and inputs.

citations.title: Hooks reference
citations.key_fact: PreToolUse hooks run after Claude creates tool parameters and before the call is processed, match built-in and MCP tool names, and can block the call (exit code 2) or return permissionDecision deny with a reason.

citations.title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
citations.key_fact: Mitigations include minimizing extension functionality and permissions and requiring human-in-the-loop approval of high-impact actions, implemented in a downstream system or the extension itself.

citations.title: alteon-sdk (Python package metadata)
citations.key_fact: alteon-sdk wraps the Alteon REST backend with configurators, management functions for facts collection and operations (for example client.api.mgmt.info.software and config commit) and deploy options dry_run, write_on_change and get_diff; minimum supported Alteon versions are 31.0.10.0 and 32.2.2.0.

citations.title: cm config-sync (tmsh reference)
citations.key_fact: run cm config-sync starts a configuration synchronization job and must be given one of to-group, from-group or recover-sync to set the direction.

citations.title: NetScaler licensing (VPX Express)
citations.key_fact: VPX Express needs no license file and offers 20 Mbps bandwidth, a maximum of 250 SSL sessions and 20 Mbps SSL throughput; from release 14.1 build 29.65 it includes all Premium-license features.

citations.title: Understanding PDIs
citations.key_fact: Personal Developer Instances are free for Developer Program members; an instance unused for ten days is reclaimed and reset, and idle instances hibernate until the owner signs in to the Developer Site.

citations.title: How Claude remembers your project (CLAUDE.md)
citations.key_fact: A project CLAUDE.md lives at ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, is shared through source control and should hold build and test commands, coding standards, naming conventions and common workflows.
